claims.claim: AUTHOR_REPAIR derives and validates task id, task revision, and base SHA from one consistent canonical underlying Run view, supporting REMEDIATION.execution.run for kind=REMEDIATION as well as ordinary primary RUNs.

Valid failed REMEDIATION RUN can receive a canonical REPAIR authorization while preserving exact failed_run_id, failed_head_sha, candidate truth, and immutable predecessor/finding lineage, eliminating the historical RUN base_sha is invalid blocker.
Missing, malformed, or contradictory REMEDIATION execution, run, base SHA, or task identity fails closed before canonical mutation, with no synthetic fallback.
Ordinary failed PRIMARY AUTHOR_REPAIR behavior, idempotency, stale selector rejection, and multi-generation supersession semantics remain behaviorally unchanged.
Existing operator, review transport, and publication REMEDIATION authorities remain untouched; no duplicate parser authority, lifecycle family, or automatic correction choice was introduced.
Focused deterministic regression reproduces the failed-remediation repair production topology and verifies canonicalization, idempotent replay, supersession, and malformed negative rejection.
Only src/aios_renew/authoring_ingress.py and tests/test_authoring_ingress.py were modified, focused verification and git diff --check passed, and zero items remain unresolved.
